COG.note: The arrete says the social registry holds data from civil-status and unique-ID systems, but states no link between the civil register and the ID system.
Nothing stated about digital civil registration.
Law 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 is only cited in the preamble; no standing, authority, regulation or application is stated.
Nothing stated about an ID number at birth; the household code is a social identification code.
Nothing stated about civil registration offices.

facts.fact: Article 8 of the joint arrete of 20 August 2024 says the registre social unique holds data drawn from the civil-status information systems and the unique identification number, among other sources.

The arrete states the registre social unique is an interoperable information system whose interoperability terms are set by separate texts, and it obliges social programmes to register beneficiaries served in it and share beneficiary information (articles 3, 17, 18).

systems.owner: Ministry of Social Affairs with Ministry of Planning and Statistics

facts.fact: The joint arrete of 20 August 2024 describes the registre social unique as a centralised web platform that registers households, generates a unique household identification code automatically and extracts potential beneficiary lists for programmes (articles 2, 5).
Article 8 of the arrete says the registre social unique holds data from the civil-status information systems and the unique identification number, among other sources.
